title: AI-accelerator S-1s ship per-counterparty risk-factor table by Q3 2026
body: By Q3 2026 the May 9 accelerator-IPO cohort weekend update — Tenstorrent's confidential S-1 draft filed under the JOBS Act EGC framework late Friday with public-filing windows opening early August and Hyundai Motor Group plus Samsung Foundry retaining co-anchor positions on the $3.4B fully-closed bridge round, SambaNova naming J.P. Morgan and Citi as joint lead bookrunners alongside Goldman Sachs for an S-1 confidential submission targeted late June at a $7-9B fully-diluted valuation range, Groq trailing 30-60 days behind pending sovereign-cloud Saudi-Arabia commitment closure, plus Bernstein's Saturday Market-Perform initiation on Cerebras CBRS at $172 citing Saudi Aramco Digital MoU dependency as the top single-counterparty concentration risk against the Morgan Stanley / Goldman / Citi Buy-rated $165-$185 cohort and the Cerebras CFO Saturday confirmation of the October 28 2026 180-day lock-up with no early-release waiver for OpenAI's $1B warrant package — combined with the SEC Corp Fin Saturday clarifying footnote treating the May 8 sample comment letter as generally applicable guidance and the same staff's standing line of inquiry on customer-concentration footnotes across the Mag-7 cohort, force the next-wave AI-accelerator S-1 cohort to standardize a single-counterparty risk-factor exhibit — a per-customer table naming counterparty, percentage-of-revenue or backlog band, contract tenor, take-or-pay language, and any sovereign-jurisdiction or export-control overlay — as the operative S-1 format rather than narrative-only disclosure. The forcing function is that once sell-side initiation on a freshly-listed comparable anchors a Market-Perform call on single-counterparty concentration, subsequent S-1 underwriters cannot let narrative-only language stand without inviting a Corp Fin comment-letter cycle that pushes the deal calendar. The likely shape is a tabular exhibit in Tenstorrent's August public-filing window, mirrored by SambaNova late June and Groq inside the same window. Bear case is a separate concept release deferring the format to 10-K disclosure; absent that, Q3 2026 lands the standardized exhibit across the cohort.

reasoning.because: Bernstein Market-Perform on CBRS anchors single-counterparty concentration as buyside marker May 9.
reasoning.given: Tenstorrent + SambaNova + Groq S-1 cohort on deck; SEC Corp Fin presses concentration footnotes.
reasoning.so_that: Accelerator-IPO S-1 filings ship a per-counterparty risk-factor exhibit with revenue-band and tenor columns.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; Tenstorrent August window first, SambaNova late June, Groq next.
reasoning.plain_language: A Wall Street analyst flagged Cerebras for leaning on one customer; upcoming chip-IPO filings will list top customers in a table.

summary: Bernstein's May 9 Market-Perform on CBRS names Saudi Aramco Digital MoU dependency as top single-counterparty risk; Tenstorrent, SambaNova, and Groq S-1 filings stack into Q3 2026. By Q3 2026 the accelerator-IPO cohort standardizes a per-counterparty risk-factor exhibit as the operative S-1 format.
